change: Limiting agentic exploration to two parameter-update iterations
reason_for_change: To compare agentic parameter exploration with and without biological evidence under the same exploration budget.

decision.reason: Current clustering shows biologically coherent markers but weak separation (low silhouette, high DBI) and several very small clusters likely representing rare PBMC populations. Increase n_neighbors to 30 to smooth the neighborhood graph and potentially improve cohesion/separation without changing resolution or PCs, enabling a clearer assessment of graph connectivity effects while preserving plausible rare populations.

Both evaluated settings (15 vs 30 neighbors at 20 PCs, res=1.0) yield similar, modest silhouette and DB; n_neighbors=30 is slightly better and biological markers suggest plausible rare DC and platelet clusters rather than spurious fragments. To seek improved separation without forcing merges, increase n_pcs to 30 to capture additional variation while holding n_neighbors and resolution constant to isolate the effect.

final_result.final_selection_reason: 1) Intrinsic metrics: Iteration 1 is marginally strongest by standard separation/cohesion criteria (highest silhouette, second-lowest Davies–Bouldin). However, the differences among all runs are very small; Iteration 0 leads WC-dispersion and Banfield–Raftery, partly offsetting its slightly higher DB and slightly lower silhouette. 2) Cluster structure: Iteration 1 has a slightly more balanced size distribution (two small clusters, modest largest-cluster fraction). Iteration 0 has three small clusters but none are extreme, and the size profile remains reasonable. 3) Biological interpretation: Iteration 0 is strongest. It resolves all expected PBMC populations (naive/central memory T, cytotoxic T, NK, B, classical and FCGR3A+ monocytes, dendritic cells, platelets) and, importantly, a small interferon-stimulated cluster (ISG15, IFI6, MX1, IFIT1, OAS1) that is a plausible rare PBMC population. In Iterations 1–2 this IFN-high group appears merged into larger lineages. 4) Final selection: Iteration 0. 5) Justification of difference from intrinsic-metric winner: Although Iteration 1 is marginally better on silhouette/DB, the gaps are negligible, while Iteration 0 captures a biologically meaningful rare IFN-high cluster without excessive fragmentation and also achieves the best WC-dispersion and Banfield–Raftery. Overall, Iteration 0 provides the strongest combined scientific evidence—competitive intrinsic quality, acceptable structure, and superior biological resolution—compared with the alternatives.
